A1.justification: Despite the changed title and substantial revision, both PDFs describe the same research lineage, retaining the shared-perturbation group-robust optimization framework. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable throughout. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes readable Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original SGDRO experiments on Waterbirds and DomainBed, together with Hessian eigenvalues and empirical loss-surface analyses. These qualify independently of the baseline results attributed to earlier work.

after.justification: v2 reports original H-CMNIST experiments, ASGDRO evaluations across multiple distribution-shift benchmarks, and Grad-CAM and Hessian analyses. Appendix D also reports domain-specific and oracle-selection results.

M1.justification: v1's SGDRO uses SAM's normalized overall-loss gradient for perturbation. v2's ASGDRO introduces ASAM's element-wise or filter-wise normalization operator, changing the perturbation geometry and training updates in Equation 2 and Algorithm 1. The shared perturbation and multiplicative group-weight updates are retained, but the adaptive component is an actual procedural change.

E1.justification: v2 adds H-CMNIST with missing-invariant-feature tests, CelebA, CivilComments toxicity classification, Multi-NLI inference, and evaluations on Camelyon17, RxRx1, FMoW, Amazon, and MetaShift. Waterbirds and four visual DomainBed datasets remain. RotatedMNIST disappears; ColoredMNIST remains under a subpopulation-shift setup rather than the earlier DomainBed evaluation.

E2.justification: The Waterbirds comparison replaces SAM with ASAM and adds IRM, IB-IRM, V-REx, CORAL, DomainMix, Fish, and LISA to the earlier ERM/GDRO comparison. DomainBed replaces the earlier algorithm panel with DPLCLIP, DPLCLIP+GDRO, and multiple backbone comparisons. Appendix C also includes LISA in the new Grad-CAM comparisons.

E3.justification: Waterbirds replaces the stated fixed rho=0.1 and method-specific L2 penalties with hyperparameter searches, including rho in {0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8}. DomainBed moves to DPLCLIP-based training and increases the reported hyperparameter-search budget from five trials to twenty. Appendix D adds test-domain validation, explicitly labeled oracle selection, alongside the retained training-domain selection approach.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled H-CMNIST tests removing color and spurious box-position cues, a two-feature Gaussian toy analysis, and Grad-CAM studies on Waterbirds and CelebA, including Appendix C. Waterbirds Hessian analysis is revised and supplemented by a CelebA group-wise Hessian comparison. v1's empirical parameter-perturbation loss curves are removed.

E5.justification: v1 reports five random seeds for Waterbirds; v2 Appendix A.6 reports three for its subpopulation experiments. The Waterbirds display loses the earlier per-group uncertainty values and reports only summary accuracies. DomainBed retains three-seed reporting and plus/minus entries, but v2 no longer explicitly identifies those entries as standard errors, as v1 did.

E6.justification: Waterbirds results are replaced: v1 Table 1 reports worst-group accuracies of 87.2% for SGDRO and 86.5% for GDRO; v2 Table 2 reports 91.0% for ASGDRO and 90.6% for GDRO. Changed methods and tuning prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains. v2 also adds extensive H-CMNIST, real-world, qualitative, and domain-specific results and replaces the earlier DomainBed and Hessian entries. New oracle results include a TerraIncognita exception: DPLCLIP+ASGDRO scores 52.2%, below DPLCLIP's 52.6%.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.1's small-rho Taylor expansion and gradient-curvature argument are removed. v2 Section 3.1 instead constructs Gaussian group-loss functions with two feature-associated parameters, explicit covariance choices, equal-group-size assumptions, and objective comparisons under different sharpness conditions. This substantially changes the mathematical justification; the new analysis is an illustrative construction with explicit assumptions.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on combining flatness and worst-group optimization while limiting the average-performance tradeoff. v2 redefines the central contribution as sufficient invariant learning, claims a connection between common flat minima and learning diverse invariant features, and introduces ASGDRO and H-CMNIST as contributions supporting that claim. This changes the scientific scope of the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds the failure-mode argument that successfully learned invariant cues can disappear at test time, and interprets GDRO's limitations as learning only a subset of available invariant features. Sections 3.2–3.3 also introduce scale-symmetry qualifications and explain how group-specific perturbations could distort sharpness comparisons and group weights. These substantially expand the earlier flatness and average-versus-worst-group interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendices A, B, and D substantially expand reproducibility information: dataset construction, model selection, architectures, optimizers, batch sizes, epochs, search ranges, group-adjustment parameters, and second-step gradient clipping. v2 also identifies reused LISA, JTT, SAM, and DPLCLIP code resources. These are substantial documentation additions beyond v1's brief settings and references, although v1's explicit Power-method description for Hessian estimation disappears.

R1.justification: v2 substantially redirects research positioning toward invariant-feature learning and general distribution shifts. It adds discussions and citations concerning SWAD, flatness-aware domain generalization, DPLCLIP, LISA, and feature learning under spurious correlations, while removing several classical DRO and SAM-efficiency references. Already-cited ASAM becomes central, and the novelty argument shifts toward sufficient invariant learning while acknowledging prior flatness-based domain-generalization research.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Sharpness-aware Minimization for Worst Case Optimization' to 'Sufficient Invariant Learning for Distribution Shift.' The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Methodology and results are reorganized around SIL, with separate subpopulation, domain-shift, real-world, and interpretability sections and new appendices organizing experimental details and extended results.

P2.justification: v1's trajectory and empirical loss-surface displays are removed. v2 adds SIL and dataset illustrations, Gaussian toy plots, benchmark and Hessian bar charts, and extensive Grad-CAM grids. Waterbirds accuracy and Hessian tables change column structure, DomainBed comparisons are redesigned, and Appendix D adds domain-specific and oracle tables. Several figures and tables also adopt side-by-side placement.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support and reproducibility. Where v1 mainly offers Waterbirds and aggregate DomainBed evidence, v2 directly tests missing-invariant-cue failure through H-CMNIST, adds feature visualizations and broader original evaluations, and documents training and model-selection procedures in Appendices A, B, and D. Reduced Waterbirds uncertainty reporting and the absence of a general proof for the SIL guarantees remain weaknesses, but the targeted diagnostic evidence and substantially improved experimental documentation provide a clear net quality gain.
